effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per structural requirement of the Mantle specification's Overview section, in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-core or logos-blockchain-ledger that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is one section of the Bedrock v1.1 Mantle specification LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot); the other sections (Mantle Transaction, Operations, Mantle Ledger, Appendix) are audited by their own briefs.

The Overview section defines the four concepts the rest of the document builds on: the Mantle transaction, Mantle operations, the Mantle ledger, and transaction fees. Its requirements are the structural statements it makes about each (what a transaction contains, what an operation is, what the ledger stores, how fees are charged). Trace those structural statements; the detailed rules belong to the other sections.

Where the structure lives in the code:
- core/src/mantle/mod.rs, src/mantle/transactions/mod.rs, src/mantle/ops/mod.rs, src/mantle/ledger.rs and src/mantle/gas.rs (package `logos-blockchain-core`): the transaction type, the operation enum, the ledger-facing transaction view, and the gas model.
- ledger/src/mantle/mod.rs and src/gas_and_fees.rs (package `logos-blockchain-ledger`): the Mantle ledger state and how fees are collected.

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id; core/src/mantle/fixtures/ shows how transactions and ledgers are built in tests. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
